steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ParentComponent with a message data property. This component will serve as the source of data to pass down.

steps.title: Create a ChildComponent that accepts props
steps.instruction: Create a new Vue component named ChildComponent that declares a prop called 'message' in its props option.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can define props in a component by adding a props option. The prop can be declared as a string array or an object with type validation.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ChildComponent is created with a 'message' prop declared in its props option.
successCriteria: ChildComponent is defined with a props option containing 'message'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ChildComponent that accepts a 'message' prop.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a ChildComponent, but make sure it declares a 'message' prop in its props option.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating a ChildComponent with a 'message' prop. Try defining the component with a props option.

steps.title: Render ParentComponent in App and pass message to ChildComponent
steps.instruction: In the App component's template, render the ParentComponent and pass the message prop to ChildComponent.
steps.hint: Use the component tag <ParentComponent> inside the template. The message prop should be passed from ParentComponent to ChildComponent.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: rendering a component and passing props
<template>
  <ParentComponent>
    <ChildComponent :message="message" />
  </ParentComponent>
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will render ParentComponent, which in turn passes the message prop to ChildComponent.
successCriteria: ParentComponent is rendered in App's template, and message prop is passed to ChildComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered ParentComponent and passed the message prop to ChildComponent, demonstrating props drilling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure ParentComponent is rendered and the message prop is passed to ChildComponent.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the template structure. Ensure ParentComponent is rendered and the message prop is passed correctly to ChildComponent.

steps.title: Display the prop in ChildComponent template
steps.instruction: In the ChildComponent's template, display the message prop using interpolation ({{ message }}) inside a paragraph element.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to output the prop value in the template.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying a prop in a Vue component template
steps.expectedOutcome: The ChildComponent will show the message passed from ParentComponent when rendered.
successCriteria: The ChildComponent template contains a paragraph element with {{ message }} interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the prop value in the child component using interpolation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the correct prop name 'message' inside double curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The prop isn't being displayed correctly. Check that you're using {{ message }} inside a paragraph element in the template.

steps.title: Create a GrandchildComponent that accepts props
steps.instruction: Create a new Vue component named GrandchildComponent that declares a prop called 'message'.
steps.hint: Define a new component with a 'props' option that includes 'message' as a string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A GrandchildComponent component is created with a 'message' prop declared.
successCriteria: The GrandchildComponent component exists and has a 'props' option containing 'message'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the GrandchildComponent with a 'message' prop. This sets up the next level for props drilling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but it might be missing the 'props' declaration or the 'message' prop. Check that your component has a 'props' option with 'message' included.
steps.feedbackWrong: The GrandchildComponent wasn't created correctly. Make sure you define a new Vue component with a 'props' option that includes 'message'.

steps.title: Add GrandchildComponent to ChildComponent and pass message prop
steps.instruction: In ChildComponent's template, render GrandchildComponent and pass the message prop to it.
steps.hint: Use the GrandchildComponent as a custom element in the template and bind the message prop to it.

steps.expectedOutcome: The GrandchildComponent will be rendered inside ChildComponent and receive the message prop.
successCriteria: GrandchildComponent is rendered in ChildComponent's template with the message prop passed down.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully passed the message prop from ChildComponent to GrandchildComponent, demonstrating props drilling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're rendering GrandchildComponent and passing the message prop to it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using the correct component name and passing the message prop properly.

steps.title: Add a button in ParentComponent to update the message
steps.instruction: In the ParentComponent template, add a button element with the text 'Update Message' that calls a method to update the message data property.
steps.hint: Add a button with a click handler that updates the message property in the component's data.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the ParentComponent that, when clicked, updates the message data property, demonstrating how prop changes flow through the component hierarchy.
successCriteria: ParentComponent template contains a button with @click handler that calls a method to update the message data property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a button that updates the message, showing how prop changes propagate through components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has a click handler that updates the message data property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or click handler is missing or incorrect. Add a button with @click that calls a method to update the message.

steps.title: Test the props drilling flow
steps.instruction: Run the app and verify that clicking the button updates the message in all nested components (ParentComponent, ChildComponent, and GrandchildComponent).
steps.hint: Click the button in ParentComponent and check if the message changes in each component's display.
steps.analogousExample:
// Testing component interaction
// After clicking a button, verify all components reflect the updated value
steps.expectedOutcome: The app runs successfully, and clicking the button updates the message displayed in all three components, demonstrating props drilling.
successCriteria: The button click updates the message in ParentComponent, ChildComponent, and GrandchildComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully observed how prop changes propagate through nested components via props drilling.
steps.feedbackPartial: The button updates the message in some components but not all. Ensure the message prop is passed correctly through each component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The message does not update in all components. Check that the button's click handler updates the message data property and that the prop is passed through each component.
